facts.claim: Anthropic's glossary describes large language models as AI models trained on very large amounts of text that can answer questions, summarize information and generate human-like text.
Anthropic's models overview states that all current Claude models accept text and image input and produce text output.
Anthropic's pricing page says its billing is based on actual monthly usage.

Anthropic's glossary says tokens are the smallest individual units of a language model and can correspond to words, subwords, characters, or even bytes; the number of characters a token represents depends on the model and the language, and token counting gives exact counts.
Anthropic's glossary describes the context window as the amount of text a language model can look back on and reference when generating new text, a working memory for the model.

Anthropic's models overview lists a 1M-token context window and a reliable knowledge cutoff of Jun 2026 for Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5, and states that base prices are given per million tokens.
OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Sol page lists a 1,050,000-token context window, a maximum input of 922,000 tokens and a Jun 01, 2026 knowledge cutoff.

Anthropic's guide to reducing hallucinations says that even the most advanced language models can sometimes generate text that is factually incorrect, a phenomenon known as hallucination, and that its techniques significantly reduce hallucinations but do not eliminate them entirely, so critical information must be validated.
Anthropic's pricing page says its billing is based on actual monthly usage.
Anthropic's guide to building evaluations says to be task-specific, designing evals that mirror the real-world task distribution and include edge cases.
Anthropic's guide to building evaluations lists irrelevant or nonexistent input data, overly long input data or user input, and poor, harmful or irrelevant user input as example edge cases.
OpenAI's quickstart describes the OpenAI API as a consistent interface to state-of-the-art AI models.

OpenAI's quickstart says to create an API key in the dashboard at platform.openai.com/api-keys, store the key in a safe location, and export it as an environment variable; it gives the macOS or Linux command export OPENAI_API_KEY and the Windows PowerShell command setx OPENAI_API_KEY.
Anthropic's quickstart says to create an API key in the Claude Console at platform.claude.com/settings/keys.
Anthropic's models overview lists the current models Claude Sonnet 5.5 with API ID claude-sonnet-5-5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 with API ID claude-haiku-5-5.
OpenAI's models page lists GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6 Luna as current models, with model IDs gpt-6.2-sol and gpt-6-luna on their model pages.
OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna page gives the model ID gpt-6-luna.
Z.AI's quick start tells you to access the Z.AI Open Platform, create a Standard API Key on the API Keys management page, and top up on the billing page if needed.
Z.AI's overview lists GLM-5.3-Flash among its featured models.
MiniMax's models page lists MiniMax-M3.1-Flash and MiniMax-M3 as its current language models.
MiniMax's API overview tells you to create a pay-as-you-go API key under API Keys with Create new secret key, and says that the subscription key for M Plan is separate from pay-as-you-go API keys.
Anthropic lets you set your own monthly spend limit below your tier's cap on the spend limits page, and requests return HTTP 400 once a spend limit you set is reached.
OpenAI's pricing page lists per-million-token prices for GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, and its spend-limits guide describes the monthly spend controls.
Anthropic's quickstart links the Claude Console page for creating an API key at platform.claude.com/settings/keys.
Anthropic's pricing page says its billing is based on actual monthly usage, and that credit card payment is accepted and purchased credits are managed on its Billing page.
OpenAI's quickstart links the dashboard page for creating an API key at platform.openai.com/api-keys.
OpenAI's quickstart links its billing overview page at platform.openai.com/account/billing/overview for adding credits.
OpenAI's spend-limits guide explains spend alerts and hard spend limits for an organization or project.
Z.AI's quick start links the API Keys management page at z.ai/manage-apikey/apikey-list, where you create a Standard API Key.
Z.AI's quick start links its billing page at z.ai/manage-apikey/billing for topping up.
Z.AI's pricing page gives prices per 1M tokens for its GLM models and states that all prices are in USD.
MiniMax's API overview links the pay-as-you-go API key page at platform.minimax.io/user-center/basic-information/interface-key, where you create a new secret key.
Anthropic's rate-limits page links the Console spend limits page at platform.claude.com/settings/spend-limits, where you can set your own monthly spend limit.
Anthropic's guide to building evaluations recommends structuring questions to allow automated grading, for example multiple-choice, string match, code-graded or LLM-graded.
Anthropic's guide to building evaluations says that more questions with slightly lower signal automated grading is better than fewer high-quality hand-graded evals.
Anthropic's guide to reducing hallucinations suggests running the same prompt multiple times and comparing outputs, because inconsistencies across outputs could indicate hallucinations.
OpenAI's quickstart tells you to store the API key in a safe location and to export it as an environment variable rather than writing it elsewhere.

Anthropic lets you set your own monthly spend limit below your tier's cap on the Console spend limits page at platform.claude.com/settings/spend-limits; when the limit is reached, requests return HTTP 400 with a message that says you have reached your specified API usage limits.
OpenAI's spend-limits guide says a spend alert sends a notification and does not stop traffic, while a hard spend limit makes affected API requests return a 429 error.
Z.AI's billing page is where you top up when needed, according to its quick start.
MiniMax's API overview says the subscription key used for M Plan is separate from pay-as-you-go API keys.
Anthropic's guide to building evaluations lists overly long input data or user input as an edge case to test.
Anthropic's rate-limits page links the Console spend limits page at platform.claude.com/settings/spend-limits, where you can set your own monthly spend limit.
Anthropic's guide to reducing hallucinations says its techniques significantly reduce hallucinations but do not eliminate them entirely, so critical information must be validated.
Anthropic's guide to building evaluations says to design evals that mirror the real-world task, to automate grading when possible, and to prioritize volume over quality.

Anthropic's guide to mitigating jailbreaks and prompt injections describes indirect prompt injection as the case where the model processes third-party content, such as webpages, emails or documents, that contains adversarial instructions.
Anthropic's guide to building evaluations says to be task-specific, designing tests that mirror the real-world task distribution and do not forget the edge cases.
